pick.name: Sole proprietorship now, Private Limited at a trigger
pick.what: Trade as yourself (PAN + Udyam + GST when needed), incorporate a Pvt Ltd when a trigger hits
pick.why: Rs 0 setup, no ROC filings or audit; keeps presumptive taxation (s.58 of Income-tax Act 2025: old 44ADA for consulting, old 44AD for SaaS/product income, see final-C); Pvt Ltd costs much more each year and needs 2 directors/shareholders
pick.free_limits: No registration fee; Udyam is free with Aadhaar + PAN

alts.name: Private Limited Company
alts.what: Limited-liability company under the Companies Act 2013
alts.why: Needed for DPIIT + 80-IAC tax holiday, equity funding and ESOPs; limited liability for healthcare/enterprise risk
alts.free_limits: Incorporation + yearly ROC filings (AOC-4, MGT-7, DIR-3 KYC) + mandatory statutory audit; legalraasta estimates ~Rs 15-30k/yr for a small company; other blogs go far higher (unverified)

alts.name: One Person Company (OPC)
alts.what: Single-member private company with limited liability
alts.why: Limited liability without a second director; since 1 Apr 2021 there is no turnover/capital cap and it can convert any time
alts.free_limits: Company-style compliance incl. audit; cannot take equity investors; OPC not named in DPIIT's official eligible list (Pvt Ltd/partnership/LLP/cooperative) and secondary sources conflict, so confirm with DPIIT

candidates.name: Sole proprietorship
candidates.verdict: PICK for now: zero overhead while revenue is small and liability is capped by contract + insurance

candidates.name: Private Limited Company
candidates.verdict: Wins once you raise money, want DPIIT/80-IAC, hire, or sign uncapped-liability enterprise/healthcare contracts

candidates.name: One Person Company
candidates.verdict: Wins only if you want limited liability now and truly have no second director; not DPIIT-eligible, must convert to raise

candidates.name: LLP
candidates.verdict: Needs 2 partners, can't issue equity/ESOPs, 30% tax per blogs; weaker than Pvt Ltd for a product company

candidates.name: Partnership firm
candidates.verdict: Unlimited liability and needs a partner; no advantage

decision: Start as a sole proprietor: it costs nothing, keeps 44ADA presumptive tax, and global SMB/B2C buyers rarely care. Incorporate a Private Limited (not OPC/LLP) on the first of: a funding conversation, the need for DPIIT/80-IAC, hiring, a healthcare/enterprise contract with uncapped liability or PHI, or revenue past the presumptive-tax limit. Verify all tax/compliance consequences with a CA.
note: Consolidated: presumptive tax is now section 58 of the Income-tax Act 2025. Consulting income falls under the old 44ADA (50% deemed profit) and SaaS/product income under the old 44AD. See the income-tax slot in the money track. Verify with a CA.
details: Sole proprietors have unlimited personal liability: cap liability in every contract (Common Paper) and buy PI cover before healthcare work. Verify with a CA/lawyer.

verify.note: Decision sound. But it says '44ADA'. final-C says presumptive tax now sits in s.58 of the Income-tax Act 2025, and SaaS/product income is 'business' (old 44AD, 6/8% of turnover), not 'profession' (44ADA, 50%). Pvt Ltd needing 2 directors/members is correct.
